body:
Global crypto markets opened August on the back foot, with total market cap sitting at $2.25T after a -0.88% drawdown over the past 24 hours and aggregate volume coming in at $54.1B. The mood is cautious but not panicked — the Fear & Greed index nudged to 27 today from 25 yesterday, a marginal improvement that still firmly reads Fear. BTC dominance holds at 56.3% and ETH dominance at 10.0%, suggesting capital remains concentrated at the top of the cap structure with limited appetite for risk rotation. The broader tone is one of consolidation fatigue: July is in the books, analysts are flagging a choppy August ahead, and the market is digesting the tail end of forced selling that characterized the final weeks of last month.

Bitcoin printed $63,087 on the session, down -1.20% over the last 24 hours and -1.30% over the past 7 days, with the 1-hour reading essentially flat at +0.10% — a signal that price is stabilizing rather than free-falling. Volume came in at $23.48B, which is meaningful but not the kind of conviction print you want to see confirming a floor. Bitcoin ETFs reportedly closed July in the green despite late-month selling pressure, which provides a constructive institutional underpinning, but spot action is telling a more hesitant story. The key level to watch is whether BTC can maintain the $63,000 handle through the weekend — a decisive break below it re-opens a retest of lower support, while reclaiming and holding above $65,000 would materially shift short-term sentiment.

ETH tracked the broader selloff with a -1.10% 24-hour decline to $1,867.63 on $7.15B in volume, though its 7-day performance of +0.70% keeps it slightly in the green on the weekly — a mild divergence worth noting against BTC's -1.30% weekly loss. The real standout is ADA, the only asset in the ZIMR tracked universe posting a positive 24-hour print at +1.30%, extending a 7-day run of +6.70% that suggests genuine rotational interest rather than noise. BNB at $585.41 is holding relative strength on the week at +3.80% despite a -0.80% daily dip. On the other end, UNI is the session's worst performer by a wide margin at -6.80% despite sitting +11.90% on the 7-day, a sharp intraday reversal that looks like profit-taking after an extended run. LINK dropped -2.10% to $8.12, XRP gave back -1.50% to $1.062 following a protocol upgrade on the XRP Ledger that restored previously pulled features, and DOT at $0.761546 remains the weakest on the weekly at -5.90%.

The macro backdrop is layered. A $70M Coldcard hardware wallet exploit — described in reporting as an attack that never touched the devices themselves — is circulating widely enough that Binance founder CZ publicly called for wallet diversification, and that headline alone is introducing a low-level security anxiety into retail sentiment. Tether posting $1.5B in operating profit for Q2 is a net positive for stablecoin credibility, though the accompanying note that its reserve buffer fell by half will attract scrutiny. The Bank of Italy's finding that stablecoins offer no consistent cost advantage for remittances chips away at one of the sector's most-cited retail use cases. The FTX distribution story — ex-users reporting funds released in a $900M round — is a meaningful overhang resolved, removing at least some technical selling pressure that had been hanging over the market. Rates and geopolitical developments are not directly cited in today's flow but the Fear reading of 27 reflects that broader macro uncertainty remains the dominant backdrop.

Looking ahead, the August setup is asymmetric and treacherous. BTC holding the $63,000 zone through the first weekend of the month is the immediate test — if forced selling is genuinely exhausted as analysts suggest, this level should act as a floor. Watching whether UNI's -6.80% session is a one-day flush or the start of a broader DeFi unwind matters given how much the 7-day rally in that pocket had run. ADA's continued outperformance deserves monitoring for whether it attracts follow-on rotation or stalls without volume backing. The Coldcard exploit story has legs — any additional details tying losses to specific custody practices could trigger a broader security narrative that weighs on retail confidence. Finally, keep an eye on whether the ETF bid that supported July's positive close sustains into August's opening week; institutional flow is the most reliable counterweight to deteriorating retail sentiment, and any softening there would be the single biggest risk to a recovery thesis.
